---
title: "Themes and options"
subtitle: "Four presets that are option dictionaries, and every key they hold."
description: "Keisen's themes, the table-options call that merges into them, and the full list of option keys by part."
---

`theme-default()`, `theme-booktabs()`, `theme-compact()`, and `theme-minimal()` each return an option dictionary, so a preset and a `table-options()` call are the same kind of thing and compose by merging.
Striping is `row-striping: true` on any of them, and the academic three-line style is `theme-booktabs()` plus options; a theme that differs by one boolean is not a theme.

Option names are Typst identifiers, so they are written unquoted: `table-options(row-striping: true)`.
An unknown key is an error rather than a silent no-op.
`tests/unit/test-options-read.typ` holds every declared key to being read by the code.
It searches the code with the comments cut out.
It looks for the key as the argument of the call that reads it, so a key named in a comment or in a message does not count.

| Group | Keys |
| --- | --- |
| Table | `table-font`, `table-font-size`, `table-align`, `table-width`, `table-border-top`, `table-border-bottom`, `breakable`, `infer-alignment`, `decimal-align`, `column-border`, `row-border` |
| Header | `header-title-size`, `header-title-weight`, `header-subtitle-size`, `header-align`, `header-border-bottom` |
| Column labels | `column-labels-align`, `column-labels-weight`, `column-labels-size`, `column-labels-border-top`, `column-labels-border-bottom`, `spanner-border-bottom` |
| Stub and groups | `stub-weight`, `stub-indent-step`, `row-group-weight`, `row-group-fill`, `row-group-border-top`, `row-group-repeat` |
| Body | `row-striping`, `row-striping-fill`, `cell-inset`, `cell-vertical-align`, `body-border-top`, `body-border-bottom` |
| Summaries | `summary-weight`, `summary-fill`, `summary-border-top`, `grand-summary-border-top` |
| Formatter defaults | `number-group-separator`, `number-decimal-separator`, `number-rounding` |
| Footer | `footer-align`, `footnote-marks`, `footnote-size`, `source-note-size`, `footer-border-top` |

: Theme options {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[25,75]"}

`table-width` is `auto`, which lets the table size itself to its content.
Given a width, the columns no `columns-width` names share whatever the named ones leave, since a track sized to its content would never fill the width.

`column-border` and `row-border` are off by default, and rule the table as a grid rather than by part.
`column-labels-align` is `auto`, which follows the column beneath the label.
`cell-vertical-align` is `auto`, which leaves the placement to Typst: a cell sits at the top of its row.
Give it `horizon` to centre every cell against the tallest one beside it, which is what a row of unequal heights usually wants.

Rules on a shared edge do not add up: the line under the column labels is the line over the body, and the line over the footer is the line under it.
A part draws its own edge, and that wins over the table's, so `body-border-top` shows only where `column-labels-border-bottom` is `none`, and `body-border-bottom` only where `footer-border-top` is.
Where the body closes the table, `table-border-bottom` claims that edge first.

`row-border` falls to every row edge the parts leave alone, which is why it draws between two body rows, between the title and the subtitle, and between two notes.
Four edges are not among them: the table's first and last, answered by `table-border-top` and `table-border-bottom`, and the body's opening and closing edges, answered by `body-border-top` and `body-border-bottom`.
On those four, `none` is an answer rather than a silence, so `row-border` never shows through.
The two body keys are `none` on every preset, and `theme-minimal` answers `none` on the table's own two as well, so a table ruled as a grid writes the rule it wants on those keys.

Which edge closes a table depends on what the table carries.
The first three below differ only in what comes last: the body itself, then a summary row, then the notes.
The fourth is a table with no notes under `theme-booktabs`, which is nothing but rules.

![Four tables showing where a rule falls. The first is titled No notes and closes with a rule under its last body row. The second is titled Summary last and closes under a bold Total row. The third is titled Notes last, carries a footnote mark on its units label, and closes under three lines of notes. The fourth has no title and carries three rules: one above the column labels, one under them, and one under the last body row.](../assets/examples/rules.png)

`number-rounding` answers a `format-number(rounding: auto)`, as `number-group-separator` and `number-decimal-separator` answer the separators, so a document sets its rounding once rather than on every directive.
